Bug: a misspelled DB_ENGINE silently starts Mealie on SQLite.

DB_ENGINE is documented to take sqlite or postgres. Any other value is quietly treated as sqlite. A typo like "postgress" therefore runs a deployment meant for Postgres on a local SQLite file, and nothing reports the mistake.

Expected: loading the settings (get_app_settings()) with any other DB_ENGINE value raises a ValueError whose message contains "DB_ENGINE", so the app refuses to start. sqlite and postgres work as before, and an unset or empty DB_ENGINE still means sqlite.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/test_config.py` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
title: fix: reject an unrecognized DB_ENGINE instead of using SQLite (#8605)
